claims.text: A machine-learning free-energy workflow can predict solid-phase free energies near fusion and at high temperatures.
The workflow can predict liquid-phase free energies near fusion and at high temperatures.
Training on a limited or sparse high-quality ab initio dataset is sufficient to construct the proposed surrogate.
The surrogate can predict complete free-energy surfaces for both solid and liquid phases.
A neural-network potential or similar surrogate can interpolate the relevant free-energy landscape from limited ab initio calculations.
The machine-learning model learns a mapping from atomic configurations to free energies.
The learned model captures vibrational entropy contributions.
The learned model captures anharmonic free-energy contributions.
The learned model captures electron–vibration coupling contributions.
Learning these contributions permits accurate free-energy prediction without extensive molecular-dynamics sampling.
The workflow can reduce computational cost by approximately an order of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD.
Predicted free energies will deviate by no more than approximately 5–10% from explicit ab initio MD or TOR-TILD results.
The workflow is intended to apply to elemental, binary, and moderate multicomponent alloy systems near their melting conditions.
Accuracy may degrade at extremely high temperatures.
Accuracy may degrade for compositions far outside the training regime.
The speed-up and accuracy will vary with system complexity and the amount of available ab initio training data.
